svg.text: Logging & Audit — Blanket Unredacted Capture, and a Stale Attribution Bug
InstantMudra Enterprises Admin Portal
⚠ AuditEntityListener always stamps "SYSTEM" — confirmed with exact code
Authentication authentication = SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication();
if (authentication != null && authentication.isAuthenticated()) return authentication.getName();
return "SYSTEM";

The real auth mechanism (AESFilter, Module 4) never populates Spring Security's SecurityContext — so this condition is never true, for any request, ever. createdBy/editedBy on every BaseEntity row are always "SYSTEM".
⚠ CRITICAL — blanket unredacted request/response capture across the entire PG & Payout vendor surface
GlobalApiLoggingAspect (@within(LoggableApi)) + VendorServiceLoggingAspect (@within(LoggableVendor))
What gets captured
request = objectMapper.writeValueAsString(args)
response = objectMapper.writeValueAsString(result)
Only non-serializable types are filtered out
(HttpServletRequest/Response, MultipartFile) —
no field-level redaction of any kind. Bank account
numbers, IFSC codes, vendor tokens, beneficiary PII —
everything is captured in full, unmasked.
Where it's applied — 13 files, confirmed by search
All 7 PG vendor impls (Razorpay, Unisus, Slpe, RunPaisa,
NixaSoft, Cashfree, Shadval) + all 4 Payout vendor impls
(Unisus, Shadval, RunPaisa, NixaSoft) + PaymentGateway-
Controller + PayoutController.
This is the default, blanket logging mechanism for
essentially the entire money-movement vendor surface —
not a one-off, like the specific leaks in Module 11.
// VendorServiceLoggingAspect, in addition to the DB write:
log.info("Vendor Service Request : {}", request); log.info("Vendor Service Response : {}", response);
Same unredacted payload written to VendorLogs (DB) AND the application log file — the same double-write leak shape confirmed in Module 11.
VendorLogs.request / .response (TEXT columns) — everything, unmasked
⚠ VendorContext.clear() only clears half of what it tracks
private static final ThreadLocal<Boolean> serviceCalled = new ThreadLocal<>();
private static final ThreadLocal<String> vendorHolder = new ThreadLocal<>();
public static void clear() { serviceCalled.remove(); } // vendorHolder is NEVER removed
Both aspects call VendorContext.clear() in their finally block after every request — but clear() only removes serviceCalled.
vendorHolder (the vendor ID) persists on the pooled servlet thread indefinitely.
On a reused thread, a later, unrelated request that never calls setVendorId() can inherit a PREVIOUS request's stale
vendor ID — mis-attributing that log entry (im_vendor_id) to the wrong vendor.
By contrast: the de-duplication between the two aspects is sound
GlobalApiLoggingAspect only saves a log row if (!VendorContext.isServiceCalled()) — so when a @LoggableVendor service
handled the request, the controller-level aspect steps aside rather than writing a duplicate row. Well-reasoned design,
independent of the redaction and ThreadLocal issues above.
Sound design, by contrast
Flagged bug
Critical — confirmed systemic unredacted-data leak
